rationale: This is a mechanical stacking of two already-tested archive signals (LiquidityBackedInnovation and IntangibleCapitalizedProfitability) into a triple rank product, which adds no new economic claim and — because multiplying three [0,1] ranks compresses almost all firms toward zero — will mostly reproduce whichever leg is most extreme rather than isolate a genuine three-way conjunction.

Debt over tangible (intangible-stripped) assets is a standard credit/collateral ratio and reduces to a plain single-theme leverage sort with a known-anomaly footprint, and the expected negative sign is not clearly supported since book leverage is also a value proxy that has historically predicted higher, not lower, returns outside acute distress.

Because TS_COUNT(xrd,5) is near-constant (5) for the overwhelming majority of R&D reporters, the multiplicative signal is dominated by MA(oancf/at,3) and is therefore effectively a rediscovery of cash-based operating profitability rather than a test of program continuity as claimed.

Retained earnings/assets is cumulative past profitability, so this is a close relabeling of the already-tested RnDCapitalTimesEarningsQuality (R&D stock × smoothed ROA, which produced a negative long-short alpha), and re/at is itself a well-known distress/quality predictor rather than a novel partner leg.

The within-firm timing dimension is a genuinely different economic claim from the archive's cross-sectional quality partners, the expression matches the hypothesis and sign, though TS_RANK over only five annual observations is coarse and the signal risks collapsing into a known earnings-momentum effect interacted with R&D intensity.

Maturity mismatch against long-duration intangible projects is an economically distinct and internally consistent claim, and the construction cleanly decomposes the earlier runway result, but the short-term-debt/rollover-risk channel is close to published debt-maturity return evidence so the incremental novelty rests entirely on the R&D interaction.
